title: KVCache attention kernel tiebreaker playbook
body:
Purpose: jot down an actionable debug/playbook for the case where attention kernel selection ties and leads to KV offset anomalies at long sequence lengths. Goal: reproduce reliably, collect traces, apply mitigation (soft/hard), and propose long-term fix.

Symptoms observed:
- Irregular KV cache wrap or stale KV reads when in-flight request sequence length > 8192 (observed around 9100–11k tokens).
- High p50 latency spikes on a subset (~3%) of requests; those correlate with unexpected kernel path (fallback to slow generic kernel) followed by KV slot reuse.
- Errors: occasional "kv_index_out_of_range" logged, and later "kv-ttl-mismatch" in metrics pipeline.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kernel selector uses rounded sequence length bucket; tie-breaker picks kernel A (fast) but its prefetch path assumes different KV layout (offset policy), causing misaligned writes when sequence crosses internal window boundary.
2) Race between eviction worker and streaming prefetch: eviction frees slot while prefetch still writing, leading to transient stale sequence indices.
3) Quantization-specific kernel variant has a different header stride, and when selected incorrectly (tiebreak), pointer arithmetic mismatch corrupts per-session KV offsets.

Repro steps (commands + notes):
- Quick repro curl to hosted test endpoint (local replay worker):
  curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer testkey' -d '{"model":"redwood/long-analyst-v2","input":"'$(python3 -c 'print("x ".join(["word"]*10000))')'","max_new_tokens":0,"stream":false}' | jq '.'
  (vary input length 8k, 9k, 11k)

- Start instrumented runtime with KVCACHE_DEBUG=1, KERNEL_SELECTOR_LOG=verbose, and EVICITON_DEBUG=1:
  env KVCACHE_DEBUG=1 KERNEL_SELECTOR_LOG=verbose EVICITON_DEBUG=1 ./bin/serve --config conf/test-tie.json

- Collect perf & heaps:
  sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- ./bin/serve --config conf/test-tie.json
  sudo perf script > perf-kernel-tiebreaker.stk

- Attach to worker when reproducing and capture memory map:
  pid=$(pgrep serve) && sudo gcore $pid && sudo cat /proc/$pid/maps > maps.$pid

Key log excerpts (sanitized):
[2025-01-30T14:12:03.223Z] selector.c:234 select_kernel: seqlen_bucket=8192 tie_candidates=[A_fast_q8, B_generic_f16] picked=A_fast_q8 reason=tiebreaker:latency_est
[2025-01-30T14:12:03.224Z] kvcache.c:987 write_kv: session=ses_43ff offset=0x7fffd1234 wrote=8192
[2025-01-30T14:12:03.225Z] eviction.c:114 try_evict: evicted_slot=ses_43ff offset=0x7fffd1234 freed=true
[2025-01-30T14:12:03.226Z] kvcache.c:1001 write_kv: session=ses_43ff offset=0x00000012 wrote=24  <-- suspicious small offset after eviction
[2025-01-30T14:12:03.227Z] trace: ERROR kv_index_out_of_range session=ses_43ff idx=9203 max_idx=8192

Experiment matrix tried so far:
- Force selector to prefer generic kernel: env SELECTOR_FORCE=generic -> no kv errors, but latency + cost increase.
- Force fast q8 kernel: env SELECTOR_FORCE=fast_q8 -> reproducible errors at >9k tokens.
- Toggle prefetch on/off: disabling prefetch reduces frequency but doesn’t eliminate failures.
- Increase eviction grace window from 2 to 16ms: failure rate drops ~70% in test bench.
- Run with quantization disabled: no failures, suggests quant kernels implicated.

Immediate mitigations (safe, short-term):
- Add defensive check in kvcache write path: if idx >= active_max_idx -> retry with lock and re-evaluate kernel selection. (cheap guard, potential perf hit)
- Bump default tie-breaker to prefer generic_f16 when seqlen > 8192 (config flag).
- Increase eviction grace period on dedicated nodes handling long-context sessions.

Investigations to run (next):
- Add structured trace around selector decision: capture candidate list, exact seqlen, hardware flags, and per-kernel header_stride. (PR: GH#repo/serving-runtime/issue/472)
- Instrument atomicity around eviction + prefetch: use sequence numbers on slots to detect concurrent ops.
- Reproduce with ASAN build of kernel variants to detect pointer arithmetic issues in quant kernel.

Tests to add/modify:
- Replay harness: generate synthetic sessions that append tokens to same session to exercise wrap boundary exactly at 8192 and +1, +16, +128. Capture kv slot meta before/after.
- Fuzz kernel selector: randomize tie-breaker policy across runs and check kvcache invariants via invariant checker (assert in debug builds).

Notes to self:
- Watch out for name collisions: "eviction" vs "eviciton" typos in logs (we have both in old branches).
- Check storage layout docs for q8 kernels: header_stride vs generic documented in /docs/kernels/strides.md (might be outdated).
- Ping Jun about index lifetime guarantees for streaming inference (possible API contract mismatch).

Open questions:
- Is this only happening on GPU type A100x with driver X.Y, or seen on T4 too? (initial data shows A100x majority).
- Could model sharding interact with kernel selection? (sessions cross-shard boundary -> slot remap?)

Next actions (assigned):
- Arielle: add lightweight guard in kvcache write and roll to staging; measure perf delta.
- Mateo: compile ASAN quant kernel build and run targeted repro.
- Jun: validate eviction scheduling codepath; add tracing for slot seq numbers.

References & quick links:
- GH PR: repo/serving-runtime/pull/472 (selector logs + guards)
- JIRA SRV-1286 (kv wrap incidents Q1)
- Internal notes: confluence/serving-runtime/kvcache-arch (see section on slot semantics)

Scratch TODOs (low friction):
- Add unit test for tie-breaker stable ordering.
- Add alert rule: if kv_index_out_of_range > 5/min then auto-toggle selector to generic for affected pool.
footer_notes: File is a personal working scratchpad. Don’t ship directly — convert to PR checklist + changelog entry before merging any guards into prod.
